verdict.rationale: Babylon.js ships its own Inspector, described as offering 'visual debugging and scene editing' and as a 'visual scene inspector', so there is a first-party visual scene-editing surface. However, it is framed mainly as a runtime debugging and analysis tool. The other visual tools (Node Material Editor, Playground code editor, Sandbox model viewer) cover shaders, code and model viewing, not level building. missing for 10: a dedicated full scene/level editor as the primary authoring workflow, a documented editor viewport, prefabs/scene-composition features, and independent hands-on evidence of building levels visually.

support.subject: As a technical artist, a full visual editor — viewport, inspector, prefabs/scene composition — is the primary way to build levels
